security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, TypeScript examples, and a relative API fetch snippet. One finding is confirmed because the workflow recommends running pnpm format, lint, type check, and tests, which can execute package scripts in a repository. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: State that pnpm commands should run only in trusted repositories and after user confirmation when scripts may execute project code.
Label shell commands as examples and separate them from TypeScript snippets to reduce automated scanner ambiguity.

content.value_statement: TypeScript projects often lose quality through weak types, inconsistent tooling, and unclear review rules. This skill provides strict typing guidance, pnpm workflow checks, TSDoc rules, and review checklists.
actual_capabilities: Recommends strict TypeScript settings and safer null handling patterns.
Guides pnpm use for formatting, linting, type checking, and tests.
Provides review checklist items for public APIs, error handling, and coverage.
Shows examples for result types, custom type guards, and async error handling.
Advises TSDoc usage for exported APIs when signatures are not enough.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automated fixes.
Does not validate a repository without tool access and project files.
Assumes pnpm is the package manager for the target project.
Focuses on TypeScript and TSX, not backend architecture or deployment.

use_cases.title: Review TypeScript Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Apply the checklist to identify weak types, missing error handling, and unclear public API documentation.

use_cases.title: Set Up Project Standards
use_cases.description: Define strict compiler settings, pnpm commands, and documentation rules for a new TypeScript project.

use_cases.title: Improve Type Safety
use_cases.description: Replace unsafe patterns with typed data structures, type guards, and safer null handling.

prompt_templates.title: Check a TypeScript File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript file for strict typing, null handling, and obvious use of any. Suggest practical fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Add TSDoc Where Needed
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these exported functions and suggest TSDoc only where the intent is not clear from the signature.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Async Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this async TypeScript flow to use clear result types, typed errors, and predictable failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Project Quality Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript quality checklist for this repository, including pnpm commands, compiler settings, testing expectations, and review gates.

output_examples.input: Review a TSX component that uses broad types and lacks a public API comment.
output_examples.output: A concise review flags the unsafe type, suggests a precise interface, and recommends TSDoc only for exported behavior.

output_examples.input: Set standards for a new TypeScript project.
output_examples.output: A practical checklist covers strict compiler settings, pnpm workflow commands, test coverage goals, and review expectations.

output_examples.input: Improve an async data loading function.
output_examples.output: A refactor plan adds typed errors, predictable result handling, and clearer null handling without adding unnecessary comments.

best_practices: Run formatting, linting, type checks, and tests before final review.
Use TSDoc for exported APIs when signatures do not explain intent.
Prefer precise types, type guards, and utility types over broad assertions.
anti_patterns: Using any in production code without a clear migration plan.
Adding comments that repeat names instead of explaining public API intent.
Running package scripts in an untrusted repository without checking what they execute.

faq.question: Does this skill run code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. Tool execution depends on the host agent and user permissions.

faq.question: Which package manager does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects pnpm and discourages npm or yarn for the target workflow.

faq.question: Can it help with TSX files?
faq.answer: Yes. The description includes TSX files, and the guidance covers TypeScript patterns used in React projects.

faq.question: Does it require strict TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends strict compiler settings and safer handling for null and undefined values.

faq.question: Will it document every function?
faq.answer: No. It recommends TSDoc for public APIs when the signature does not explain the intent.

faq.question: Is it suitable for security reviews?
faq.answer: Only for TypeScript quality checks. It is not a substitute for a dedicated security audit.
